name: Ipng
description: IPng (IP Next Generation): the historic candidate protocols TUBA, PIP, SIPP and TP/IX

rfc1347.title: TCP and UDP with Bigger Addresses (TUBA), A Simple Proposal for Internet Addressing and Routing
rfc1347.abstract: This paper describes a simple proposal which provides a long-term solution to Internet addressing, routing, and scaling.  This memo provides information for the Internet community.  It does not specify an Internet standard.

rfc1385.title: EIP: The Extended Internet Protocol
rfc1385.abstract: EIP can substantially reduce the amount of modifications needed to the current Internet systems and greatly ease the difficulties of transition.  This is an "idea" paper and discussion is strongly encouraged on Big-Internet@munnari.oz.au.  This memo provides information for the Internet community.  It does not specify an Internet standard.

rfc1454.title: Comparison of Proposals for Next Version of IP
rfc1454.abstract: This is a slightly edited reprint of RARE Technical Report (RTC(93)004).  This memo provides information for the Internet community.  It does not specify an Internet standard.

rfc1475.title: TP/IX: The Next Internet
rfc1475.abstract: This memo presents the specification for version 7 of the Internet Protocol, as well as version 7 of the TCP and the user datagram protocol.  This memo defines an Experimental Protocol for the Internet community.  It does not specify an Internet standard.

rfc1476.title: RAP: Internet Route Access Protocol
rfc1476.abstract: This RFC describes an open distance vector routing protocol for use at all levels of the internet, from isolated LANs to the major routers of an international commercial network provider.  This memo defines an Experimental Protocol for the Internet community.  It does not specify an Internet standard.

rfc1526.title: Assignment of System Identifiers for TUBA/CLNP Hosts
rfc1526.abstract: This document describes conventions whereby the system identifier portion of an RFC 1237 style NSAP address may be guaranteed uniqueness within a routing domain for the purpose of autoconfiguration in TUBA/CLNP internets.  This memo provides information for the Internet community.  It does not specify an Internet standard.

rfc1561.title: Use of ISO CLNP in TUBA Environments
rfc1561.abstract: This memo specifies a profile of the ISO/IEC 8473 Connectionless-mode Network Layer Protocol for use in conjunction with RFC 1347, TCP/UDP over Bigger Addresses.  It describes the use of CLNP to provide the lower-level service expected by Transmission Control Protocol and User Datagram Protocol.  This memo defines an Experimental Protocol for the Internet community.  This memo does not specify an Internet standard of any kind.

rfc1621.title: Pip Near-term Architecture
rfc1621.abstract: The purpose of this RFC and the companion RFC "Pip Header Processing" are to record the ideas (good and bad) of Pip.  This memo provides information for the Internet community.  This memo does not specify an Internet standard of any kind.

rfc1622.title: Pip Header Processing
rfc1622.abstract: The purpose of this RFC and the companion RFC "Pip Near-term Architecture" are to record the ideas (good and bad) of Pip.  This memo provides information for the Internet community.  This memo does not specify an Internet standard of any kind.

rfc1710.title: Simple Internet Protocol Plus White Paper
rfc1710.abstract: This document was submitted to the IETF IPng area in response to RFC 1550.  This memo provides information for the Internet community.  This memo does not specify an Internet standard of any kind.

rfc1768.title: Host Group Extensions for CLNP Multicasting
rfc1768.abstract: This memo provides a specification for multicast extensions to the CLNP protocol similar to those provided to IP by RFC1112.  This memo defines an Experimental Protocol for the Internet community.  This memo does not specify an Internet standard of any kind.

rfc3598.title: Sieve Email Filtering -- Subaddress Extension
rfc3598.abstract: On email systems that allow for "subaddressing" or "detailed addressing" (e.g., "ken+sieve@example.org"), it is sometimes desirable to make comparisons against these sub-parts of addresses.  This document defines an extension to the Sieve mail filtering language that allows users to compare against the user and detail parts of an address. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc5233.title: Sieve Email Filtering: Subaddress Extension
rfc5233.abstract: On email systems that allow for 'subaddressing' or 'detailed addressing' (e.g., "ken+sieve@example.org"), it is sometimes desirable to make comparisons against these sub-parts of addresses.  This document defines an extension to the Sieve Email Filtering Language that allows users to compare against the user and detail sub-parts of an address. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc6848.title: Specifying Civic Address Extensions in the Presence Information Data Format Location Object (PIDF-LO)
rfc6848.abstract: New fields are occasionally added to civic addresses.  A backward- compatible mechanism for adding civic address elements to the Geopriv civic address format is described.  A formal mechanism for handling unsupported extensions when translating between XML and DHCP civic address forms is defined for entities that need to perform this translation.  Initial extensions for some new elements are also defined.  The Location-to-Service Translation (LoST) protocol mechanism (defined in RFC 5222) that returns civic address element names used for validation of location information is clarified and is normatively updated to require a qualifying namespace identifier on each civic address element returned as part of the validation process. [STANDARDS-TRACK]

rfc8981.title: Temporary Address Extensions for Stateless Address Autoconfiguration in IPv6
rfc8981.abstract: This document describes an extension to IPv6 Stateless Address Autoconfiguration that causes hosts to generate temporary addresses with randomized interface identifiers for each prefix advertised with autoconfiguration enabled.  Changing addresses over time limits the window of time during which eavesdroppers and other information collectors may trivially perform address-based network-activity correlation when the same address is employed for multiple transactions by the same host.  Additionally, it reduces the window of exposure of a host as being accessible via an address that becomes revealed as a result of active communication.  This document obsoletes RFC 4941.

rfc9873.title: Additional Email Address Extension for the Extensible Provisioning Protocol (EPP)
rfc9873.abstract: The Extensible Provisioning Protocol (EPP) does not inherently support internationalized email addresses because the specifications for these addresses did not exist when EPP was developed.  This document describes a command-response extension that adds support for associating an additional email address with an EPP contact object.  That additional email address can be either an internationalized email address or an ASCII-only address.
